title: Facial Recognition & Biometric Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Protect yourself from facial recognition surveillance and biometric data collection with this comprehensive privacy security checklist.
intro: Facial recognition technology is everywhere - from social media to retail stores to government surveillance. This checklist helps you protect your biometric privacy and reduce your exposure to unwanted face scanning and data collection.

items.task: Disable facial recognition on social media platforms
items.why: Platforms like Facebook and Google Photos use facial recognition to identify you in photos, building detailed profiles of your appearance and associations.
items.howTo: Go to Facebook Settings > Face Recognition and turn off. In Google Photos, disable face grouping in Settings. Check similar settings on Instagram, Twitter, and other platforms you use.

items.task: Review and remove existing photo tags of yourself
items.why: Previous facial recognition tagging has already created biometric profiles that can be used to identify you in future photos.
items.howTo: Use Facebook's Activity Log to review all photos you're tagged in. Remove tags or request friends delete photos. Do the same for other social platforms where you appear.

items.task: Minimize uploading clear photos of your face
items.why: Every clear facial photo you share online can be used to train facial recognition systems and identify you elsewhere.
items.howTo: Before posting photos, consider if your face is clearly visible. Use sunglasses, masks, or creative angles. Focus on scenery or group shots where faces are less prominent.

items.task: Consider disabling Face ID/facial unlock on devices
items.why: Law enforcement can compel you to unlock devices with your face, and biometric data may be stored or transmitted to third parties.
items.howTo: On iPhone, go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode and disable. On Android, go to Settings > Security > Face Unlock and turn off. Use strong PINs or passwords instead.

items.task: Audit camera permissions for installed apps
items.why: Many apps request camera access and could potentially use facial recognition without your knowledge.
items.howTo: Check Settings > Privacy > Camera (iOS) or Settings > Apps & Notifications > Permission Manager > Camera (Android). Remove camera access for apps that don't need it.

items.task: Turn off automatic photo syncing to cloud services
items.why: Cloud services often analyze uploaded photos with facial recognition, even if you haven't explicitly enabled it.
items.howTo: Disable iCloud Photos, Google Photos backup, OneDrive photo sync, and similar services. Manually backup important photos to local storage instead.

items.task: Wear masks, sunglasses, or hats in public when appropriate
items.why: Physical barriers can prevent facial recognition systems in stores, streets, and public venues from identifying you.
items.howTo: Wear sunglasses with wide frames, face masks, or hats that partially obscure your face. Be aware of local laws and social norms regarding face coverings.

items.task: Research and avoid stores known to use facial recognition
items.why: Major retailers use facial recognition for loss prevention and marketing, building profiles of your shopping habits and movements.
items.howTo: Check online databases of stores using facial recognition. Look for posted signs about biometric collection. Shop at smaller, local businesses that are less likely to use such technology.

items.task: Use cash payments when possible to avoid linking face to identity
items.why: When facial recognition is combined with payment data, stores can build detailed profiles linking your appearance to your identity and purchases.
items.howTo: Carry cash for routine purchases. If using cards, consider prepaid cards purchased with cash to add a layer of anonymity to your transactions.

items.task: Learn about biometric privacy laws in your area
items.why: Some jurisdictions have strong biometric privacy protections that give you rights to control how your facial data is collected and used.
items.howTo: Research laws like Illinois' BIPA, California's CCPA, and GDPR if in EU. Understand your rights to opt-out, delete data, and file complaints with regulators.

items.task: Send opt-out requests to companies that may have your biometric data
items.why: Many companies must honor opt-out requests, and some will delete existing biometric data if you ask.
items.howTo: Contact major tech companies, retailers you frequent, and data brokers to request removal from facial recognition databases. Use privacy-focused browsers like Incognito Browser when researching and submitting requests.

items.task: Stay informed about biometric data breaches
items.why: When biometric databases are breached, your facial data could be exposed permanently since you cannot change your face like a password.
items.howTo: Set up alerts for biometric data breaches. Follow privacy news sources and consider joining class-action lawsuits when appropriate to hold companies accountable.
